clue.text: After losing heart, gained miss

indicators.note: the middle of the word for gained drops out, as a body loses its heart

parts.note: to have netted something is to have gained or captured it

explanation.surface: Someone who, though dispirited by a setback, still came away with a gain they had been missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the scene; the heart of NETTED is its central pair TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to feel its lack, which is to want or require it.

clue.text: Upturn in crime receiving penalties — time inside? Smart behaviour

indicators.note: the reversed word receives the rest within it
in a down clue an upturn reads the word from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the word for penalties

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties

explanation.surface: A rise in crime brings fines and prison terms — is that clever conduct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'time inside' suggests a prison sentence; here it says where T goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Niftiness is deftness or cleverness, the quality of being smart and neat in action.

clue.text: Editor: "Not remade, edited!"

indicators.note: something edited has been altered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor insists the piece was only edited, not rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendator is one who emends texts, correcting and improving them as an editor does.

clue.text: Old guy's drug habit repelled Henry

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine
a habit is a regular use or practice

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: An elderly man's drug habit drove off his friend Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Old guy stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah, said in Genesis to have lived 969 years, is the byword for an extremely aged person.

clue.text: American philosopher, the writer accepted by old monarch and child

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun is taken into the monarch's letters

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of Queen Elizabeth
the setter refers to themself as the writer, giving me
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A writer is welcomed by an aged king and his child.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the nineteenth-century American essayist and leader of Transcendentalism.

clue.text: Milliner's product brought about passion to secure new headwear

indicators.note: the headwear is brought about, or around, the other letters

parts.note: a hat is headwear

indicators.note: the passion word holds the new letter fast within it

parts.note: ire is angry passion

explanation.surface: A hat-maker's creation stirred strong feelings by holding a new hat in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' reads like 'caused' in the surface but signals going around.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine net worn over the hair to keep it in place, a milliner's sort of item.

clue.text: Small fish at the surface for a change

parts.note: hake is a food fish of the cod family
up describes something risen to the surface

explanation.surface: A little fish rises to the surface for a change of scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a thorough reorganisation, so a major change.

clue.text: Learning about Italy's foremost river

indicators.note: the learning word goes about, or around, the letter

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional learning

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first

parts.note: the first letter of Italy's

explanation.surface: Studying the chief river of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at an Italian river, but the answer is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Convenient limitations on heredity?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: useful and close at hand
second meaning, read cryptically: the limits of the word heredity are its end letters ..., so '...'

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: the first and last letters of heredity are H and Y, and saying 'H and Y' spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is conveniently within reach or useful.

clue.text: Payment getting daughter a meal?

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: Does a daughter receive a meal in return for a payment?
explanation.definitionFit: A feed is an informal noun for a hearty serving of food, as in having a good feed.

clue.text: Negotiation about college drugs, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for negotiation goes about, or around, the college letter

parts.note: mediation is negotiation carried out through a go-between

explanation.surface: Talks are held about a university's policy on drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication covers medicines generally; drugs are one example, which the 'perhaps' acknowledges.

clue.text: Sabbath withdrawing from song prize

indicators.note: the Sabbath letter withdraws, leaving the song word without it

parts.note: a psalm is a sacred song

explanation.surface: A hymn loses its Sunday slot and wins an award.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm was the ancient symbol of victory, so it stands for a prize or honour, as in bearing the palm.

clue.text: I support province, after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror reverses, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: aid is help or support
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it over and decides to back a regional cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: India is the radio-alphabet code word for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet each letter has a code word, and the letter I is spoken as India.

clue.text: Expressing honesty after that time with bank

parts.note: since means from that time onward
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Someone has been candid ever since dealing with their bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something sincerely is to say it genuinely, with honest feeling.

clue.text: Men sit and eat abroad — here?

definitions.text: Men sit and eat abroad — here?

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men sitting down to a meal in a foreign country — where would that be?
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two pieces of fodder. Read whole, the clue also describes the place itself: a small French bar-café where men sit and eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar, a typical place to sit and dine in France.

clue.text: Breakfast food for one German

parts.note: e.g., for example, is used for 'for one'

explanation.surface: Breakfast food served to a single German.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg, boiled or fried, is a staple of the cooked breakfast.

clue.text: In favour of demonstration?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone supports a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' suggests a protest, but here it means showing something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a demonstration that establishes the truth of a claim, as in mathematics.

clue.text: Nasty — that's clear? Not very — no mark of error acquired

indicators.note: the remaining word acquires the new letters within it
not very means the very letter is left out

parts.note: 'obvious!' is said when something is plain to see
taken as written
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's nasty report: the work is not very clear, yet carries no crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or offensive.

clue.text: Fellow unknown in France misrepresented English as uncommitted

indicators.note: the unknown letter goes in the word France
something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A mysterious man in France misrepresented the English as having no loyalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone not attached to any lover, free of romantic commitment.

clue.text: Stone applied to untreated cornstalk

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
raw means in its natural, unprocessed state

explanation.surface: A weight is laid on a stalk of corn that has not been processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is the dried stalks of cereal crops left after threshing.

clue.text: Orwellian hero secures a good deal

parts.note: to win something is to secure it
tons means a great deal, informally

explanation.surface: A hero from Orwell lands a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Smith is the protagonist of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Ancient king, name not supplied, engaging courageous leader of men

indicators.note: the outer word engages, or takes in, the other pieces

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, marks a work whose author's name is not given
game means plucky and willing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of men

explanation.surface: An ancient king, his name unrecorded, recruits a brave commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Cordial article is probing solution to first clue

indicators.note: the word is probes into, or enters, the first clue's solution

parts.note: the first clue is 1 Across, whose solution is need
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly piece of writing investigates the answer to the opening clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as friendly, but it is the noun: a sweet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed flavours several cordials and liqueurs, such as anisette, so it names such a drink.

clue.text: One assisting some gambling in rising course

indicators.note: the wager goes in the reversed word
in a down clue rising reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a rota is a rotation or set course of turns
a bet is a single piece of gambling

explanation.surface: A helper places a bet on a racecourse that is going uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor is someone who aids or encourages another, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Energy of charred remnants — hydrogen extracted without difficulty

indicators.note: the hydrogen letter is extracted, or pulled out

parts.note: ashy means made of or like ashes

explanation.surface: Energy is drawn from burnt residue by removing hydrogen with no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy is used as an adverb meaning without effort, as in take it easy or easy does it.

clue.text: Granted, I may be embraced by blade, a romantic type

indicators.note: the pieces are held within the word for blade, as in an embrace

parts.note: a vane is a blade of a windmill or propeller
something lent has been granted for temporary use
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sword-wielding suitor admits he might be swept into an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a sweetheart chosen or courted on St Valentine's Day, so a romantic partner.

clue.text: Place planet not entirely close to Neptune

indicators.note: the planet is not given in full, so its last letter goes

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of Neptune

explanation.surface: Position a planet near, but not quite on top of, Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event happens.

clue.text: Begin handing out a meal

indicators.note: the a is handed out, so it is given away and removed

parts.note: to launch is to begin or set going
taken as written

explanation.surface: Start serving a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Pen capturing 'nine' as top score in darts?

indicators.note: the pen captures, or encloses, the numeral

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A darts player's pen marks down nine as the best score.
explanation.walkthrough: The top score with one dart is treble twenty; the question mark admits that a full turn can make more.
explanation.definitionFit: A single dart in the treble-twenty bed scores the most any one dart can, three times twenty.

clue.text: Note the inn conjecturally around part of golf-course here?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the golf-course part
a conjecture is guesswork, so these letters are arranged by guess into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a tee is the area each hole is played from

explanation.surface: Someone guesses an inn might lie somewhere around the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, so the whole clue points to it as 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar the nineteenth hole, the place they go after the eighteenth.

clue.text: Not quite all the senses: taste John overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so it is removed

parts.note: flavour is the taste of something
john and lav are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: John's sense of taste was ignored, so he did not have all his senses.
explanation.definitionFit: There are traditionally five senses, so one short of the full set is this number.

clue.text: Modern ice melting, penetrated by hot sea creature

indicators.note: the hot letter pierces into the rearranged letters
melting ice loses its shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Present-day ice is melting under heat, threatening marine life.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinoderms are the marine phylum of starfish, sea urchins and sea cucumbers.

clue.text: I fish, nothing less — plenty of water round here!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish
O looks like a zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An angler on a small island boasts that they fish and nothing else, surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a piece of land with sea on every side.
